paper.title_en: Multi-client Delegated Verifiable Blind Quantum Computing
paper.abstract_en: We construct a multi-Client verifiable blind delegated quantum computing (VBDQC) protocol in which M classical Verifier Clients jointly delegate a public quantum circuit acting on their combined private inputs to two quantum-capable Provers sharing entanglement but having no direct communication channel. We begin by modifying the single-Client, entanglement-based CGJV Verifier-on-a-Leash protocol. We then prove simulator-based blind verifiability for the modified protocol using the abstract/constructive cryptography framework. We adapt the DFPR upward-reduction chain to the two-Prover setting, constructing a no-direct-communication simulator architecture. We then extend the CGJV protocol to M Clients using classical multiparty computation techniques, preserving the single-Client guarantees of completeness, soundness, and blindness while additionally guaranteeing input privacy between Clients. Security is analyzed under a threat model that allows a subset of Clients to collude with one but not both of the Provers, which do not communicate even after the protocol execution.
